summary: Burst of 5xx errors after global config sweep — runtime restart loops and API failures
description:
Issue summary:
Customers observed a sudden burst of 5xx responses (502/503) across multiple NovaDocs tenants in us-east following a global configuration sweep at ~2026-03-10T09:45Z. The API gateway returned upstream 502/503; behind the gateway several serving-runtime pods entered a fast restart loop and produced OOM/gpu-mmap errors in kube logs.

Impact:
- ~12% increased 5xx rate for NovaDocs over a 25-minute window, causing degraded user-facing document generation.
- Short-lived elevated latency for all streaming sessions; some streaming sessions terminated with connection reset.
- Customer workspace on dedicated capacity experienced reduced throughput until mitigation applied.

Environment:
- Prod cluster: gke-us-east-prod-3
- Region: us-east-1
- Customer tier: enterprise (dedicated pool pinned to redwood-v1-medium)

Steps to reproduce / timeline:
1) 2026-03-10T09:44Z: config-service roll-out initiated — global batch/concurrency policy change (increase max_concurrent_infers from 8 to 16, change prefetch target ratio).
2) 2026-03-10T09:45Z: config sweep completed and new policy applied to target tenants including NovaDocs.
3) 2026-03-10T09:46Z: first 502s observed by API gateway health monitors for NovaDocs route.
4) 2026-03-10T09:50–10:10Z: multiple serving-runtime pods for the dedicated pool OOM/killed and restarted; kubelet logs show repeated gpu memory fragmentation warnings and device mmap failure.
5) 2026-03-10T10:02Z: Support contacted; mitigation (rollback policy -> previous batch/concurrency) started at 10:08Z.
6) 2026-03-10T10:20Z: 5xx rate returned near baseline; pods stabilized by 10:35Z.

Recent config changes associated:
- max_concurrent_infers: 8 -> 16
- batch_latency_target_ms: 10 -> 50
- aggressive prefetch enabled for pinned models

Logs / evidence (key excerpts):
- api-gateway: upstream_err="502" upstream_addr="10.24.5.12:8080" request_id=rn-3e1c
- kubelet pod/runtime: "OOMKilled" status, dmesg: "nvmap: mmap failed - mmap_device_io failed"
- runtime stderr: "KVCache::realloc failed, fragmentation detected, attempted fallback kernel; watchog_reset()"
- monitoring: GPU mem util sudden drop to 20% followed by repeated allocation spikes and then GPU driver ENOMEM events.

Investigation notes:
- Correlated the timing of the global config sweep with the start of error surge; all impacted runtime pods received updated batching/concurrency flags via config-service.
- Hypothesis: increasing concurrency and batch_latency_target allowed more inflight requests to accumulate on dedicated GPUs that already had fragmented KV cache state, triggering fallback kernel paths that are sensitive to contiguous device memory. That led to allocation failures, watchdog resets, and pod restarts.
- Autoscaler did not add nodes quickly because pods were restarting before new capacity could be scheduled; backpressure amplified at api-gateway leading to 502s.
- Not a network/TLS issue — connection logs show normal handshake; failures are from upstream process exit.

Mitigation applied:
- Rolled back config sweep for affected tenant group at 2026-03-10T10:08Z (reverted max_concurrent_infers and prefetched disabled).
- Temporarily increased pod restart backoff and hysteresis to avoid thundering restarts while kube drains were happening.
- Throttled incoming rate at API gateway for NovaDocs for 20 minutes via route weight reduction to give serving-runtime time to recover.

Resolution / current status:
- After rollback and gateway throttling, runtime pods stopped restarting and 5xx returned to baseline by 2026-03-10T10:35Z.
- Customer reports partial service degradation resolved; no data loss.

Follow-up actions / owners:
- Engineering (runtime team) to add safety cap in config-service that prevents doubling concurrency for pinned/dedicated pools without preflight simulation (Owner: @Luca Martinez; due 2026-03-17).
- Runtime team to add diagnostics to detect KVCache fragmentation and trigger a graceful fallback before kernel swap (Owner: @Priya Shah; due 2026-03-24).
- SRE to add a short delay/rolling-apply strategy for config sweeps that affect pinned dedicated pools (Owner: @Noah Kim; due 2026-03-14).
- Support to contact NovaDocs CSM and schedule a post-incident review (Owner: @Asha Rao; due 2026-03-12).

Notes:
- Linked to prior incidents involving model prefetch amplification (see SUP-51234) and rollout-induced 5xx waves (see SUP-214890).
- No billing or invoice impact recorded.
